listening.en: Over the summer, the empty courtyard became a garden before our eyes as neighbours planted and watered it.
listening.zh: 夏天期間，鄰居種植及澆水，空院子就在我們眼前變成花園。
listening.promptZh: 說話者怎樣知道院子的改變？

options.en: They saw the change taking place over time.
options.zh: 他們看着改變隨時間發生。

options.en: They heard a description years after leaving the neighbourhood.
options.zh: 他們離開社區多年後聽到描述。

options.en: The garden had already disappeared before anyone could see it.
options.zh: 任何人看見前，花園已消失。

options.en: They watched a recording of the completed garden after all the work had finished.
options.zh: 全部工作完成後，他們看了已成花園的錄影。

listening.explanationZh: before our eyes 指直接看着改變；不是工作完成後才聽描述或看完成景象的錄影。

reply.promptZh: 你們怎樣體驗空院子變成花園的過程？
reply.promptEn: How did you experience the courtyard becoming a garden?

options.en: We watched the neighbours plant it over the summer.
options.zh: 我們看着鄰居在夏天種植。

options.en: It changed before our eyes.
options.zh: 它就在我們眼前改變。

options.en: We saw new plants appear as the work progressed.
options.zh: 工作進行時，我們看見新植物逐漸出現。

options.en: We followed the changes in person rather than hearing about them later.
options.zh: 我們親身見證變化，而非之後才聽說。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述直接見證；金句使用 before our eyes。

scene.promptZh: 你每天經過社區中心，看着空牆由底稿逐步變成壁畫。哪句貼切？

options.en: I learned about the completed mural only from a later report.
options.zh: 我只從後來報告得知完成的壁畫。

options.en: The mural was removed before I ever saw it.
options.zh: 我還未見過壁畫，它便已移除。

options.en: The mural took shape before my eyes.
options.zh: 壁畫就在我眼前逐漸成形。

scene.explanationZh: 每天看着施工是直接見證，不是事後聽聞或從未看見。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不符合 before our eyes？

options.en: We watch a demonstration change a material in front of us.
options.zh: 我們看着示範令材料在眼前改變。

options.en: We learn years later about an event nobody in our group witnessed.
options.zh: 我們多年後才得知一件組內無人見證的事件。

options.en: We repeatedly observe a familiar place changing over several weeks.
options.zh: 我們幾星期內反覆觀察熟悉地方改變。

contrast.explanationZh: 沒有直接見證、只事後得知，不是眼前發生的意思。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友用 before our eyes 後，便說自己已知道改變的所有原因。哪句回應較準確？

options.en: Watching a change tells us it happened, but we may still need evidence about its causes.
options.zh: 看着改變讓我們知道它發生，但原因仍可能需要證據。

options.en: Seeing the finished garden is enough to establish the full reason for each change.
options.zh: 看見完成的花園，已足以確定每項改變的全部原因。

options.en: We can report our first explanation as confirmed without checking the process.
options.zh: 我們可以不查過程，就把最初解釋報作已證實。

dialogue.explanationZh: 直接觀察與完整因果解釋不同；不能以見證取代查證原因。

speaking.en: The empty room became a workshop before our eyes.
speaking.zh: 空房間就在我們眼前變成工作坊。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述親眼見證的改變。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你們每天看義工把空房間整理成閱讀角，看見書架、座椅與書本逐步加入。用一至兩句英文描述直接見證。

examples.en: We watched the work each day, and the reading corner took shape before our eyes.
examples.zh: 我們每天看着工作，閱讀角就在眼前逐漸成形。

takeaways.en: The plan became a real exhibition before our eyes.

takeaways.en: We saw the familiar landscape change before our eyes.
takeaways.zh: 我們看着熟悉景觀就在眼前改變。

titleEn: do most of the heavy lifting
titleZh: 完成最費力的主要工作

brief.meaningEn: Perform the largest or most demanding share of the work, often without physical lifting.
brief.meaningZh: 完成工作中最大或最吃力的部分，常不涉及實際搬重物。
brief.grammar: do the heavy lifting; do most of/all the heavy lifting; do more of the heavy lifting compares shares. Share all the heavy lifting means divide the entire demanding workload; more is comparative, not necessarily most.
brief.boundaryZh: 本課是主要費力工作的比喻，不保證其餘工作不重要；most、all、more 指不同份額，需按原句保留。 原資料469的 all 保留「全部」，不照抄同列把它說成大部分的概括。
brief.misconceptionZh: 工具做了大量處理，不等於人不用檢查結果；也不只看誰最後展示成果。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出誰或甚麼完成主要工作，並保留其他參與者的責任。

options.zh: 它完成了初步分類中最費力的大部分工作。

options.en: It handled the time-intensive sorting that would otherwise be manual.
options.zh: 它處理原本要人手做的費時分類。

options.zh: 它減少了義工要做的例行處理。

scene.promptZh: 資料整理中，一位組員先核對並分類幾千項資料，其他人再編排展示及檢查例外。哪句有根據？

options.en: Her main contribution means the presentation and all exception checks were already complete.
options.zh: 她的主要貢獻表示展示及所有例外查核也已完成。

scene.explanationZh: 幾千項核對分類是主要費力部分；其他人仍有展示及例外查核工作。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論最不宜由 did most of the heavy lifting 得出？

options.en: The person or tool handled a large demanding share of the work.
options.zh: 該人或工具處理了大而費力的工作份額。

options.en: No other work remains and no one else has a responsibility.
options.zh: 沒有其他工作，也沒有其他人需要負責。

options.en: The wording may be figurative rather than physical lifting.
options.zh: 說法可比喻工作，而非實際搬重物。

contrast.explanationZh: most 不等於全部；主要工作完成後仍可能需要查核或其他步驟。

options.en: Could we judge the software’s work only by how quickly the final slide appears?
options.zh: 我們可否只按最後投影片出現多快，評價軟件工作？

options.en: It handles most of the processing, but uncertain cases still need our review.
options.zh: 它處理大部分工序，但不確定個案仍需我們覆核。

dialogue.explanationZh: 工作份額大不表示每一步都已完成；要保留題目提到的覆核。

speaking.en: The software does most of the heavy lifting, while we review unusual cases.

options.en: The new chair has taken the reins.
options.zh: 新主席已接手掌管。

options.en: The former chair still makes every main decision as before.
options.zh: 舊主席仍如之前作每項主要決定。

scene.explanationZh: 新任接手帶領，與舊任作顧問是角色轉移，不是仍由舊任全權主導。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個角色最不像 take the reins？

options.en: A new coordinator takes over the main direction of an event.
options.zh: 新協調員接手活動主要方向。

options.en: A deputy becomes responsible for organising the team after the leader leaves.
options.zh: 領袖離開後，副手開始負責組織團隊。

options.en: A visitor observes the meeting without taking control or responsibility.
options.zh: 訪客旁觀會議，沒有接手控制或責任。

contrast.explanationZh: 單純旁觀而沒有接手帶領，不是 take the reins。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友用 take the reins 形容舊主席把控制交給新人，你想釐清方向。哪句最有用？

options.en: Who is taking control, and who is handing it over?
options.zh: 誰正在接手控制，誰正在交出？

options.en: Could we describe both people as stepping down without checking their new roles?
options.zh: 我們可否不查新角色，便說兩人都退下來？

options.en: Should the visitor be called the new leader simply because they attended?
options.zh: 訪客只因出席，是否就應稱新領袖？

dialogue.explanationZh: 先分清交出與接手，才能選 take 或 hand over；出席本身也不等於接任。

speaking.en: She has taken the reins of the project while the former leader advises the team.
speaking.zh: 舊領袖向團隊提供意見時，她已接手掌管項目。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再區分接手帶領者與提供意見者。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：校報主編畢業後，你接手安排截稿與編輯會議，前主編仍願意提供意見。用一至兩句英文說明接任。
writing.selfCheckZh: 說清楚自己接手帶領，前主編提供意見；不改成前任仍掌握所有決定。

examples.en: I have taken the reins of the school paper and will coordinate deadlines and editing meetings.
examples.zh: 我已接手掌管校報，會協調截稿及編輯會議。

examples.en: After the editor graduated, I took the reins while she continued to offer advice.
examples.zh: 主編畢業後，我接手掌管，她則繼續提供意見。

takeaways.en: The new coordinator took the reins when the project restarted.
takeaways.zh: 項目重新開始時，新協調員接手掌管。

takeaways.en: Taking the reins means accepting responsibility for directing the work.
takeaways.zh: 接手掌管表示承擔帶領工作的責任。

titleZh: 主要由機器運作或帶動

brief.meaningEn: Operated, controlled or shaped mainly by machines rather than direct manual effort.
brief.meaningZh: 主要由機器而非直接人手操作、控制或帶動。
brief.grammar: a machine-driven process; become increasingly machine-driven; compound adjective.
brief.boundaryZh: 主要由機器帶動不表示完全沒有人的角色；可仍需設定、監察與覆核。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不只指房間內有一部機器，也不是每項使用電腦的活動都完全自動。
brief.outcomeZh: 能根據主要操作方式描述流程，保留人手實際責任。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Book 1 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The factory has become increasingly machine-driven.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 27, table 2, row 5; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: The production line became more machine-driven, while staff still adjusted the settings and checked the output.
listening.zh: 生產線變得較由機器帶動，員工仍調整設定並核對成品。
listening.promptZh: 生產方式有甚麼改變？

options.en: Machines handled more of the operation, while people retained specified tasks.
options.zh: 機器處理較多操作，人們保留已指明的工作。

options.en: People assembled every part manually without machines.
options.zh: 人們不用機器，人手裝配每部分。

options.en: The presence of one unused computer was the only change described.
options.zh: 唯一描述的改動是一部未使用的電腦在場。

options.en: The staff stopped checking the output once machines were introduced.
options.zh: 引入機器後，員工停止核對成品。

listening.explanationZh: more machine-driven 說明主要操作方式改變；while 保留員工設定及查核。

reply.promptZh: 引入新設備後，工場流程怎樣不同？
reply.promptEn: How has the workshop process changed since the new equipment was introduced?

options.en: The machines now carry out more of the routine operation.
options.zh: 機器現在執行較多例行操作。

options.en: Staff spend more time supervising settings than assembling each part.
options.zh: 員工花較多時間監察設定，而非裝配每部分。

options.en: The process is more machine-driven, though people still check the result.
options.zh: 流程較由機器帶動，但人們仍查核結果。

options.en: More steps are performed automatically, with workers handling adjustments.
options.zh: 更多步驟自動執行，工人處理調整。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述機器角色增加但仍有人手工作；金句使用 machine-driven。

scene.promptZh: 一條包裝線主要由機器分流及封裝，人員則監察、調整設定。哪句有根據？

options.en: It is a manual process with no machinery involved.
options.zh: 它是沒有機器參與的人手流程。

options.en: It is largely machine-driven, with staff monitoring it.
options.zh: 它主要由機器運作，人員負責監察。

options.en: It is called machine-driven only because a computer sits unused nearby.
options.zh: 它稱作由機器運作，只因旁邊放着未用的電腦。

scene.explanationZh: 主要分流封裝由機器做，支持流程描述；不是只有機器擺在旁邊。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項資料最不足以支持 machine-driven？

options.en: Machines perform most routine processing while people monitor.
options.zh: 機器做大部分例行處理，人們監察。

options.en: Automated equipment controls the main assembly sequence.
options.zh: 自動設備控制主要裝配次序。

options.en: A machine is present but unused while people do every operational step by hand.
options.zh: 有機器在場但未使用，人們人手完成每項操作。

contrast.explanationZh: 機器在場不等於機器帶動流程，需看實際操作角色。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友把 machine-driven 翻成「完全沒有員工」，但原句說員工仍核對成品。哪句建議最準確？

options.en: Keep the machines’ main operational role and the workers’ remaining checks in the translation.
options.zh: 翻譯時保留機器的主要操作角色及工人餘下的查核。

options.en: Remove the checking clause so the translation is simpler.
options.zh: 刪去查核分句，令翻譯較簡單。

options.en: Treat the machine as unused because people are still present.
options.zh: 因有人在場，就把機器當作未使用。

dialogue.explanationZh: 主要由機器帶動與人手查核可並存；不能刪去實際責任或否定機器角色。

speaking.en: The process is increasingly machine-driven, but staff still review the output.
speaking.zh: 流程越來越由機器帶動，但員工仍覆核成品。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再描述機器主導與人手覆核的共存。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區洗衣服務改由大型洗衣機完成主要清洗，職員仍按布料分類、放入衣物及核對取衣安排。用一至兩句英文描述機器與人員角色。

examples.en: The laundry service is now more machine-driven, with large washers doing the cleaning while staff sort the fabrics and organise collection.
examples.zh: 洗衣服務現在較由機器帶動，大型洗衣機負責清洗，職員則按布料分類並安排取衣。

examples.en: Although the cleaning is machine-driven, people still load the washers and check that each customer receives the right clothes.
examples.zh: 雖然清洗由機器帶動，人們仍需放入衣物，並核對每位客人拿到正確衣物。

writing.selfCheckZh: 明確寫主要清洗由機器完成，人仍分類及核對，不把 machine-driven 說成無人參與。

takeaways.en: The workshop uses a machine-driven process with human supervision.
takeaways.zh: 工場使用由機器運作、人手監察的流程。

takeaways.en: Machine-driven production can still require careful human checks.
takeaways.zh: 由機器帶動的生產仍可能需要仔細人手查核。

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese translations checked against each English sentence; not independent human approval.

brief.meaningEn: Depend on a person, service, resource or method for something needed.
brief.meaningZh: 依靠某人、服務、資源或方法，取得需要的支援。
brief.grammar: rely on + noun/pronoun; rely on someone to do something; relied, relying.
brief.boundaryZh: 本課是基本依賴關係，不一定互相依靠；第113課 rely on one another 特別強調雙向互助。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可同時依靠不止一個來源；依靠某工具不表示不需核對或自己思考。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出依靠的具體來源及它提供的必要支援。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Book 1 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Earlier generations relied on hand tools for this work.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 27, table 2, row 6; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: Before the new database, the club relied on a paper register to track equipment loans.
listening.zh: 新資料庫出現前，社團依靠紙本登記冊追蹤器材借用。
listening.promptZh: 紙本登記冊有甚麼角色？

options.en: It was a display item that the club never used.
options.zh: 它是社團從未使用的展品。

options.en: It was the method the club depended on for tracking loans.
options.zh: 它是社團追蹤借用時所依靠的方法。

options.en: It was an optional reference that the club kept while using another main record.
options.zh: 它是社團另用主要紀錄時保留的非必要參考。

options.en: It was introduced only after the new database was fully working.
options.zh: 它只在新資料庫完全運作後才引入。

listening.explanationZh: before new database 說明時間；relied on 指紙本登記冊作追蹤所依靠的方法。

reply.promptZh: 新資料庫還未有時，社團怎樣掌握借用紀錄？
reply.promptEn: How did the club keep track of loans before the new database?

options.en: We used a paper register as the main record.
options.zh: 我們用紙本登記冊作主要紀錄。

options.en: We depended on written entries to see who had each item.
options.zh: 我們依靠書面項目查看誰持有器材。

options.en: We relied on a paper register to track the loans.
options.zh: 我們依靠紙本登記冊追蹤借用。

options.en: The handwritten list was our source for checking current loans.
options.zh: 手寫清單是我們查核現有借用的資料來源。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都提供具體方法；金句使用基本 rely on 框架，不必是雙向互助。

scene.promptZh: 你沒有自己的車，每週參加排練都靠公共交通。哪句準確？

options.en: I rely on public transport to get to rehearsals.
options.zh: 我依靠公共交通去排練。

options.en: I drive my own car to every rehearsal.
options.zh: 我每次都開自己的車去排練。

options.en: I use public transport only for leisure trips, not to reach rehearsals.
options.zh: 我只在遊玩時用公共交通，不用來去排練。

scene.explanationZh: 依靠的方向是自己需要交通去排練，不是自己駕車，也不是只用於遊玩。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不符合 rely on a register to track loans？

options.en: A team uses the register as its main record of who borrowed items.
options.zh: 團隊用登記冊作借用人的主要紀錄。

options.en: A register stays unused on a shelf while all tracking is done through a different system.
options.zh: 登記冊放在架上未用，所有追蹤都透過另一系統。

options.en: People consult the register to find which equipment is still out.
options.zh: 大家查登記冊找出哪些器材仍借出。

contrast.explanationZh: 未使用而全部依靠另一系統，不是依靠這本登記冊追蹤。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說 rely on a tool 就等於不用自己查核輸出。哪句較準確？

options.en: Use the tool’s result without reviewing the entries marked uncertain.
options.zh: 不覆核標示不確定的項目，直接用工具結果。

options.en: Stop using the tool altogether before finding out which parts need checking.
options.zh: 未查哪些部分需核對，就完全停用工具。

options.en: We can rely on it for routine processing and still check uncertain results.
options.zh: 我們可以依靠它做例行處理，仍查核不確定結果。

dialogue.explanationZh: 依靠工具的某項支援與人手覆核可並存，不需全收或全拒。

speaking.en: We rely on the shared register to track equipment loans.
speaking.zh: 我們依靠共用登記冊追蹤器材借用。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出具體依靠的來源與用途。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你出門一周，陽台植物需人澆水，一位已答應的鄰居會照顧，你先把不同植物的需要寫清楚。用一至兩句英文說明依靠的人及準備。

examples.en: I will rely on my neighbour to water the plants while I am away, so I have written down their different needs.
examples.zh: 我離家期間會依靠鄰居澆植物，所以已寫下它們不同需要。

examples.en: My plants rely on the help of a neighbour during my week away; I will leave clear notes about their care.
examples.zh: 我離家一周期間，植物要靠鄰居幫忙；我會留下清楚照顧筆記。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把人、支援及出門時段說清，不把依靠誤作已不需交代照顧需要或雙方互相依靠。

takeaways.en: We relied on the paper record before the database was ready.
takeaways.zh: 資料庫未準備好前，我們依靠紙本紀錄。

takeaways.en: You can rely on a useful tool while still checking important details.
takeaways.zh: 你可以依靠有用工具，同時仍核對重要細節。

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese translations checked against each English sentence; not independent human approval.

titleEn: run on both engines and algorithms
titleZh: 同時依靠機械與數碼系統

target.pattern: \brun(?:s|ning)? on both engines and algorithms\b|\bran on both engines and algorithms\b

brief.meaningEn: Depend on physical machinery and computational rules working together.
brief.meaningZh: 同時依靠實體機械與運算規則共同運作。
brief.grammar: an operation runs on both engines and algorithms; both A and B emphasises two inputs.
brief.register: Contextual machinery-and-computing metaphor, not an opaque fixed idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: engines 代表機械動力，algorithms 代表數碼規則；不是軟件完全取代實體設備，也不是所有決定都必定自動。
brief.misconceptionZh: both 要保留兩方面作用；只有機械或只有計算，均未完整表達這個比較。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體動力及路線/排序規則解釋兩方面協作。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Book 1 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.expression: runs on both engines and algorithms
sources.sentence: Modern manufacturing runs on both engines and algorithms.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 28, table 1, row 2; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: Our fictional delivery operation runs on both engines and algorithms: vehicles move the parcels, while software plans the routes.
listening.zh: 我們虛構的送貨運作同時依靠機械與運算規則：車輛運送包裹，軟件規劃路線。
listening.promptZh: 句子如何解釋兩者？

options.en: Vehicles handle the transport, but routes are chosen manually without software.
options.zh: 車輛負責運輸，但路線人手選擇，沒有軟件。

options.en: Software only records completed journeys rather than planning where vehicles go.
options.zh: 軟件只記錄已完成旅程，而不是規劃車輛去哪裏。

options.en: Vehicle movement and software route planning have different supporting roles.
options.zh: 車輛移動與軟件路線規劃扮演不同支援角色。

options.en: The account describes digital planning but leaves the physical transport role unmentioned.
options.zh: 描述只提數碼規劃，未提實體運輸角色。

listening.explanationZh: 冒號後分別說出實體移動與數碼規劃，支持 both 的兩方面。

reply.promptZh: 虛構送貨流程為甚麼不只靠車輛？
reply.promptEn: Why does the fictional delivery process depend on more than vehicles?

options.en: Software also helps decide the routes.
options.zh: 軟件也幫忙決定路線。

options.en: It runs on both engines and algorithms, combining transport with route planning.
options.zh: 它同時依靠機械與運算規則，結合運送與路線規劃。

options.en: The vehicles provide movement, but digital rules organise where they go.
options.zh: 車輛提供移動，數碼規則則安排去哪裏。

options.en: The plan depends on computing as well as physical transport.
options.zh: 計劃不只依靠實體運輸，也依靠運算。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都回應兩方面協作；金句完整使用比喻組合。

scene.promptZh: 虛構貨運場有機械搬運貨物，也有軟件分配移動路線；兩者共同維持運作。哪句貼切？

options.en: The operation runs on both engines and algorithms.
options.zh: 運作同時依靠機械與運算規則。

options.en: The software displays routes that staff have already chosen manually.
options.zh: 軟件顯示職員已人手選好的路線。

options.en: The vehicles operate independently while software only stores the completed journey records.
options.zh: 車輛獨立運作，軟件只儲存已完成旅程紀錄。

scene.explanationZh: 題目給出機械搬運及軟件分配的雙重角色；軟件不只是顯示人手已選路線或事後儲存紀錄。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個描述最未完整呈現 both engines and algorithms？

options.en: Machinery moves items while digital rules coordinate routes.
options.zh: 機械移動物件，數碼規則協調路線。

options.en: Vehicles provide transport alongside software planning.
options.zh: 車輛提供運輸，另有軟件規劃。

options.en: Only the physical machinery is described, with no computational role mentioned.
options.zh: 只描述實體機械，沒有提到運算角色。

contrast.explanationZh: both 要有機械與運算兩面，只描述其中一面未完整。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友把這句概括成「軟件取代車輛」，你想保留兩種角色。哪句最準確？

options.en: The software plans the routes; the vehicles still carry the parcels.
options.zh: 軟件規劃路線；車輛仍運送包裹。

options.en: We can treat a finished route plan as if the parcels have already been transported.
options.zh: 我們可以把路線規劃完成，當作包裹已運送。

options.en: We should describe vehicle transport alone and leave out the software’s coordination.
options.zh: 我們應只描述車輛運送，省略軟件協調。

dialogue.explanationZh: 數碼規劃與實體運送互相配合，不應把其中一項當作取代全部工作。

speaking.en: The delivery operation runs on both engines and algorithms.
speaking.zh: 送貨運作同時依靠機械與運算規則。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再保留 both 所指出的兩種支援。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：課堂虛構農場由收割機引擎帶動實際收割，軟件根據已給生長資料選擇先收哪片田；人員仍監察。用一至兩句英文概括機械動力與運算分工，不提供實際操作指引。

examples.en: The fictional harvest runs on both engines and algorithms: machines cut the crops while software selects the fields using growth data.
examples.zh: 虛構收割運作同時依靠引擎與運算：機器收割作物，軟件則用生長資料選擇田區。

examples.en: Our imagined farm runs on both engines and algorithms, combining powered harvesters with data-based field choices under human supervision.
examples.zh: 我們想像的農場同時依靠引擎與運算，把有動力收割機與依資料選田結合，並由人員監察。

writing.selfCheckZh: 保留引擎實際帶動與軟件選田兩個角色，不把規劃本身說成已收割或省去人員監察。

takeaways.en: The operation runs on both engines and algorithms, combining movement with coordination.
takeaways.zh: 運作同時依靠機械與運算規則，結合移動與協調。

takeaways.en: A system that runs on both engines and algorithms needs physical equipment as well as digital rules.
takeaways.zh: 同時依靠機械與運算規則的系統，需要實體設備，也需要數碼規則。

brief.meaningZh: 以人手工作，而非自動或機器操作流程完成。
brief.grammar: write/make/sew/assemble something by hand; may still use simple hand tools.
brief.boundaryZh: 人手可以拿筆、針或手工具，不等於完全不用工具；重點在主要操作方式。
brief.misconceptionZh: 人手不自動表示品質較好或較差，也不等於慢到不能完成；要按情況描述。
brief.outcomeZh: 能清楚比較人手與機器方法，不把手工具錯當自動化。

listening.en: She wrote the labels by hand with a pen instead of using the label printer.
listening.zh: 她用筆人手寫標籤，而沒有用標籤打印機。
listening.promptZh: 她如何製作標籤？

options.en: She used a pen to write them manually.
options.zh: 她用筆人手寫。

options.en: She typed them and printed them with the label printer.
options.zh: 她打字後用標籤打印機印。

options.en: She asked the printer to reproduce a stored file automatically.
options.zh: 她讓打印機自動重印已儲存檔案。

options.en: The phrase says she used no tool of any kind, including a pen.
options.zh: 片語表示她完全沒用任何工具，包括筆。

listening.explanationZh: with a pen 明確顯示可用手工具；by hand 對比打印機的製作方式。

reply.promptZh: 標籤打印機未能使用時，你怎樣做標籤？
reply.promptEn: How did you make the labels when the label printer was unavailable?

options.en: I used a pen and wrote each one myself.
options.zh: 我用筆，自己逐張寫。

options.en: I made them manually instead of printing them.
options.zh: 我人手做，而不是打印。

options.en: I wrote the labels by hand.
options.zh: 我人手寫標籤。

options.en: I filled in the cards with a pen before attaching them.
options.zh: 貼卡前，我先用筆填寫。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明人手製作；金句用 by hand。

scene.promptZh: 你用針線自己縫好書袋，而不是用縫紉機。哪句準確？

options.en: I made it with an automated sewing machine.
options.zh: 我用自動縫紉機製作。

options.en: I sewed the bag by hand.
options.zh: 我人手縫了書袋。

options.en: I guided the fabric through a powered sewing machine to make the bag.
options.zh: 我用電動縫紉機導引布料，製成書袋。

scene.explanationZh: 針線可用作人手縫製；by hand 不排除簡單工具。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個做法最不符合 by hand？

options.en: Writing a card with a pen.
options.zh: 用筆寫卡。

options.en: Sewing a small repair with a needle and thread.
options.zh: 用針線縫補一小處。

options.en: Having an automated machine assemble each item without manual assembly.
options.zh: 讓自動機器裝配每件物品，沒有手動裝配。

contrast.explanationZh: 自動裝配與人手完成的方法不同；拿筆或針仍可是 by hand。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友以為 by hand 表示不能用筆，你要澄清。哪句最準確？

options.en: A pen is a hand tool; writing manually can still be done by hand.
options.zh: 筆是手用工具；人手寫作仍是 by hand。

options.en: We should call pen writing automated because a tool is involved.
options.zh: 因涉及工具，我們應把用筆寫稱為自動化。

options.en: The neater finished card must have been machine-printed, regardless of how it was made.
options.zh: 無論實際怎樣做，較整齊的成品必定是機器印的。

dialogue.explanationZh: 重點在操作方式，不是是否有任何工具或外觀。

speaking.en: We wrote the invitations by hand instead of printing them.
speaking.zh: 我們人手寫邀請卡，而不是打印。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再比較人手與機器製作方式。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：烘焙課沒有用攪拌機，你用雙手搓麵團，旁邊仍會用碗及刮刀盛放材料。用一至兩句英文描述製作方式，不比較誰較高級。

examples.en: I kneaded the dough by hand rather than using a mixer, with a bowl and scraper nearby.
examples.zh: 我用雙手搓麵團，沒有用攪拌機，旁邊仍有碗與刮刀。

examples.en: We prepared the dough by hand in the baking class; using a bowl did not make it an automated process.
examples.zh: 烘焙課中我們用人手處理麵團；用碗不會令它變成自動化流程。

writing.selfCheckZh: 描述雙手搓麵團與不用攪拌機，容許簡單工具，不把 by hand 寫成完全無工具。

takeaways.en: The cards were written by hand with a pen.
takeaways.zh: 卡片用筆人手寫成。

takeaways.en: A simple tool can still be used when something is made by hand.
takeaways.zh: 人手製作時，仍可使用簡單工具。

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese translations checked against each English sentence; not independent human approval.

titleZh: 需要大量時間的人力工作

brief.meaningEn: Work done by people that requires a substantial amount of time.
brief.meaningZh: 由人完成、需要花大量時間的工作。
brief.grammar: require/reduce time-consuming human effort; effort is uncountable in this sense.
brief.register: Transparent descriptive noun phrase in process discussions.
brief.boundaryZh: 費時不等於無價值或不準確；工具可能減少部分工作，但仍要看哪些人手步驟不可省。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是只說任務等待很久，也不是把任何人的短暫參與都叫大量費時工作。
brief.outcomeZh: 能具體描述人手重複或核對工序的時間要求，不直接推成應全部取消。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Book 1 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Automation has reduced the need for time-consuming human effort.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 28, table 1, row 4; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: Copying each old record into the new list required time-consuming human effort, so the team tested a tool for the repetitive parts.
listening.zh: 把每項舊紀錄抄進新清單需要大量費時人力，所以團隊為重複部分測試工具。
listening.promptZh: 團隊想改善哪部分？

options.en: Time spent waiting for an automatic transfer, without anyone copying the records.
options.zh: 等待自動轉移的時間，沒有人抄錄紀錄。

options.en: The repetitive manual copying that took considerable time.
options.zh: 花很多時間的反覆人手抄錄。

options.en: The only quick check that people made after every task was automated.
options.zh: 全部工作自動化後，人們唯一做的快速查核。

options.en: A short review after the records had already been copied automatically.
options.zh: 紀錄已自動抄錄後的一次簡短覆核。

listening.explanationZh: copying each old record 指具體人手工序；time-consuming 說明大量時間，不是等候自動轉移或已自動完成後的簡短覆核。

reply.promptZh: 你們為甚麼想測試抄錄工具？
reply.promptEn: Why do you want to test a copying tool?

options.en: Manual copying takes a large amount of the team’s time.
options.zh: 人手抄錄佔團隊大量時間。

options.en: We want to reduce repetitive data entry while keeping checks.
options.zh: 我們想減少重複輸入，同時保留查核。

options.en: The existing process requires time-consuming human effort.
options.zh: 現有流程需要大量費時人力。

options.en: A tool may handle repeated entries so people can focus on doubtful cases.
options.zh: 工具可能處理重複項目，讓人專注有疑問個案。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋測試工具的時間與分工理由；金句描述現有工序。

scene.promptZh: 組員逐行把幾千項資料從舊表抄到新表，做了多個下午，還需核對。哪句準確？

options.en: The copying involves time-consuming human effort.
options.zh: 抄錄涉及大量費時人力。

options.en: The work is only an automatic transfer that requires no manual copying.
options.zh: 工作只是自動轉移，沒有手動抄錄。

options.en: People only reviewed the finished list after a program had copied all the records.
options.zh: 程式抄完全部紀錄後，人們只覆核完成清單。

scene.explanationZh: 逐行抄錄與多個下午支持費時人手工作，不是自動抄錄或只在自動完成後覆核。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以描述 time-consuming human effort？

options.en: People manually copy thousands of entries over several days.
options.zh: 人們幾天內人手抄錄數千項目。

options.en: A tool completes the transfer automatically while a person makes one brief check.
options.zh: 工具自動完成轉移，一人只作一次簡短查核。

options.en: Volunteers spend many sessions matching old records by hand.
options.zh: 義工花很多節時間，人手比對舊紀錄。

contrast.explanationZh: 自動轉移加簡短查核，未呈現大量費時的人力工序。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說費時人力就表示沒有價值，你想區分效率與必要查核。哪句最合理？

options.en: We should remove the uncertain-case review before finding out what it prevents.
options.zh: 未查不確定個案覆核能防止甚麼，就先刪去它。

options.en: Let us judge the result only by how little human time it takes.
options.zh: 我們只按用了多少人手時間來評價結果。

options.en: Some repetitive work can be reduced, while necessary human checks may still be valuable.
options.zh: 有些重複工作可減少，但必要人手查核仍可有價值。

dialogue.explanationZh: 時間需求與價值不是同一判斷；應分清重複工序與必要查核。

speaking.en: The old process required time-consuming human effort to copy each record.
speaking.zh: 舊流程需要大量費時人力，逐項抄錄紀錄。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出人手工序及花費時間的原因。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：劇團要修復多套舊戲服，義工需逐件檢查磨損、補縫及整理，做了多個下午。用一至兩句英文說明這些人手工作費時，並建議合理分配時段。

examples.en: Restoring the worn costumes requires time-consuming human effort, so the volunteers need a realistic schedule for checking and mending each piece.
examples.zh: 修復破舊戲服需要大量費時人力，所以義工需有合理時間表，逐件檢查及補縫。

examples.en: The careful inspection and mending involve time-consuming human effort; dividing the work across several afternoons would help the group plan its time.
examples.zh: 仔細檢查與補縫涉及大量費時人力；把工作分到幾個下午，有助小組規劃時間。

writing.selfCheckZh: 指出具體人手檢查與補縫及所需時段，不只說等待很久，也不因費時就貶低工作價值。

takeaways.en: The repetitive task required time-consuming human effort.
takeaways.zh: 重複工作需要大量費時人力。

takeaways.en: Reducing time-consuming human effort should not remove necessary checks.
takeaways.zh: 減少大量費時人力，不應取消必要查核。

titleEn: sit at the crossroads of science and ethics
titleZh: 處於科學與倫理的交會點

target.pattern: \bsit(?:s|ting)? at the crossroads of science and ethics\b|\bsat at the crossroads of science and ethics\b

brief.meaningEn: Involve scientific questions together with moral questions about what should be done.
brief.meaningZh: 同時涉及科學問題與應如何行動的道德問題。
brief.grammar: an issue/proposal sits at the crossroads of A and B; explain both fields.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是地理十字路口，也不只是兩科名稱相鄰；需指出科學方法與道德責任如何共同影響決定。
brief.misconceptionZh: 有技術能力不等於已回答應否採用；道德疑慮也不表示無需理解方法。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分別指出一個科學問題與一個倫理問題，以及兩者的連繫。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Book 1 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.expression: sits at the crossroads of science and ethics
sources.sentence: Animal testing sits at the crossroads of science and ethics.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 28, table 2, row 2; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: The fictional photo-study proposal sits at the crossroads of science and ethics: researchers want useful data, but participants must understand how their images would be used.
listening.zh: 虛構相片研究提案處於科學與倫理交會點：研究者想取得有用資料，但參加者需明白相片會如何使用。
listening.promptZh: 提案為甚麼涉及兩方面？

options.en: It concerns only the method’s accuracy, with participants’ choices outside the decision.
options.zh: 它只關乎方法準確度，參加者選擇不在決定範圍。

options.en: The data question is linked to how participants are informed and treated.
options.zh: 資料問題與如何告知及對待參加者相連。

options.en: Researchers plan to explain the image use only after the study has ended.
options.zh: 研究者計劃在研究結束後才解釋相片用途。

options.en: Participants’ understanding has already been verified, leaving only the technical comparison to consider.
options.zh: 參加者理解已獲確認，只剩技術比較需要考慮。

listening.explanationZh: 有用資料是研究考量，相片使用的理解是倫理考量；兩者共同影響提案。

reply.promptZh: 虛構相片研究為甚麼不只是技術問題？
reply.promptEn: Why is the fictional photo study more than a technical question?

options.en: Participants need to understand what will happen to their images.
options.zh: 參加者需明白相片之後會怎樣處理。

options.en: The method must be considered alongside responsibilities to the people involved.
options.zh: 方法需連同對相關人士的責任考慮。

options.en: It sits at the crossroads of science and ethics.
options.zh: 它處於科學與倫理的交會點。

options.en: Useful data does not by itself settle whether the proposed use is acceptable.
options.zh: 資料有用本身，未能決定提議用途是否可接受。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明技術之外的責任；金句用交會點比喻。

scene.promptZh: 學生提案要比較影像辨識方法，也要決定如何讓參加者明白及選擇相片用途。哪句貼切？

options.en: The proposal sits at the crossroads of science and ethics.
options.zh: 提案處於科學與倫理的交會點。

options.en: The proposal compares accuracy while leaving image use entirely outside the review.
options.zh: 提案只比較準確度，把相片用途完全排除在檢視之外。

options.en: The technical comparison removes the need to consider participants’ choices.
options.zh: 技術比較免除了考慮參加者選擇的需要。

scene.explanationZh: 方法比較與參加者選擇共同構成科學及倫理考量，不是只談技術，或把技術成效當作已取代參加者責任。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個內容最未完整呈現 crossroads of science and ethics？

options.en: A method is assessed for research usefulness and treatment of participants.
options.zh: 評估方法的研究用途及對待參加者的方式。

options.en: The discussion considers data quality alongside informed choices about image use.
options.zh: 討論連同相片用途的知情選擇，考慮資料品質。

options.en: Only the technical accuracy is described, with no moral question raised.
options.zh: 只描述技術準確度，未提出道德問題。

contrast.explanationZh: 只提科學技術一面，未完整呈現與倫理交會的兩方面。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說方法有效，就已解決研究倫理問題。哪句回應較準確？

options.en: Treat the accuracy result as a substitute for asking how the images may be used.
options.zh: 把準確結果當作詢問相片可怎樣使用的替代品。

options.en: We still need to consider participants’ understanding and choices as well as the method’s performance.
options.zh: 除了方法表現，我們仍需考慮參加者的理解與選擇。

options.en: We can explain the use of images after the study rather than before participants choose.
options.zh: 我們可以研究後才解釋相片用途，而非在參加者選擇前說明。

dialogue.explanationZh: 技術成效與倫理責任是相關而不同的問題；不能由方法有效就替代後者。

speaking.en: The proposal sits at the crossroads of science and ethics.
speaking.zh: 提案處於科學與倫理的交會點。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再用交會點比喻同時涉及的兩類問題。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：虛構研究想測試一件社區珍藏舊布料的染料，但取樣會移除一小部分。小組既要考慮分析價值，也要讓擁有者明白損失並作選擇。用一至兩句英文描述科學與倫理交會，不提供實際取樣或法律指引。

examples.en: The dye study sits at the crossroads of science and ethics: useful analysis must be weighed alongside the owners’ understanding of the material that would be removed.
examples.zh: 染料研究位於科學與倫理交會處：有用分析需與擁有者對將被移除材料的理解一併考慮。

examples.en: This proposal sits at the crossroads of science and ethics because testing the treasured textile also raises questions about the owners’ choice and the loss of material.
examples.zh: 提案位於科學與倫理交會處，因為測試珍藏布料也涉及擁有者選擇與材料損失。

glossary.en: the material that would be removed

writing.selfCheckZh: 同時寫分析價值及所有者理解材料損失與選擇，不由有用結果取代倫理考量。

takeaways.en: Some research sits at the crossroads of science and ethics.
takeaways.zh: 有些研究處於科學與倫理的交會點。

takeaways.en: A proposal that sits at the crossroads of science and ethics needs both technical and moral examination.
takeaways.zh: 處於科學與倫理交會點的提案，需要技術與道德兩方面檢視。

english.evidence: Read every model, option and example for sense, grammar, contextual fit and target morphology; not independent human approval.

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese translations checked against each English sentence; not independent human approval.

brief.meaningEn: Dismiss a concern, request or argument without giving it proper consideration.
brief.meaningZh: 未充分考慮就把疑慮、要求或論點擱在一旁。
brief.grammar: brush aside a concern; brush it/them aside with pronouns.
brief.boundaryZh: 與仔細考慮後有理由不採納不同；本課不是把實物掃到旁邊。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不同意不一定是忽略；關鍵是有沒有真正聽取、查看及回應。
brief.outcomeZh: 能區分未考慮就擱置與有理由的評估。

sources.sentence: The welfare concerns should not be brushed aside.

listening.en: The committee brushed aside the request for a quiet area without reading the explanation from the participants.
listening.zh: 委員會未讀參加者的解釋，就把設安靜區的要求擱置。
listening.promptZh: 委員會如何處理要求？

options.en: It examined the explanation and gave a detailed reason for its decision.
options.zh: 它查看解釋，並詳細說明決定理由。

options.en: It dismissed the request before considering the participants’ reasons.
options.zh: 它未考慮參加者理由就把要求擱置。

options.en: It asked for more information before making a decision.
options.zh: 它先要求更多資料才決定。

options.en: It approved the quiet area and began arranging it.
options.zh: 它批准安靜區，並開始安排。

listening.explanationZh: without reading 表示未充分考慮便擱置，不是經評估後不採納。

reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼認為委員會未公平考慮要求？
reply.promptEn: Why do you think the committee did not consider the request fairly?

options.en: The explanation was not read before the decision.
options.zh: 作決定前沒有讀解釋。

options.en: Participants were not given a chance to explain the need.
options.zh: 參加者未獲機會解釋需要。

options.en: The committee brushed aside the request without examining it.
options.zh: 委員會未檢視就把要求擱置。

options.en: The response did not address the reasons that had been submitted.
options.zh: 回應沒有處理已提交的理由。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出缺乏適當考慮；金句用本課片語描述。

scene.promptZh: 組員提出現有時間讓部分人無法出席，負責人未看回饋就說不用再談。哪句準確？

options.en: The concern was brushed aside without proper consideration.
options.zh: 疑慮未獲充分考慮就被擱置。

options.en: The feedback was compared with all the available times before a reasoned decision.
options.zh: 先比較回饋與所有可用時間，再有理由作決定。

options.en: The organiser asked affected members to clarify which times would work.
options.zh: 主辦者請受影響組員說明哪些時間可行。

scene.explanationZh: 未看回饋便停止討論是擱置，不是查看後評估或要求釐清。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個做法最不符合 brush aside a concern？

options.en: Dismissing a request before reading the explanation.
options.zh: 未讀解釋就擱置要求。

options.en: Listening carefully, checking the evidence and explaining why the proposal cannot be used.
options.zh: 仔細聆聽、查核證據，並解釋為何不能採用提案。

options.en: Telling people not to raise the issue again without addressing their reasons.
options.zh: 未回應理由就叫大家別再提出問題。

contrast.explanationZh: 經適當考慮後不採納，可與未聽便擱置不同。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「沒有同意我的提案，就一定是 brushed aside」。哪句澄清最準確？

options.en: We should judge only by whether the final decision was yes.
options.zh: 我們應只按最後是否答應來判斷。

options.en: Could we ignore the written reasons because the outcome was disappointing?
options.zh: 結果令人失望，我們可否不看書面理由？

options.en: Did they consider and respond to your reasons, even if they did not agree?
options.zh: 即使沒有同意，他們有沒有考慮及回應你的理由？

dialogue.explanationZh: 是否充分考慮不同於是否同意；需看處理過程與理由。

speaking.en: We should examine the request, not brush it aside without reading it.
speaking.zh: 我們應檢視要求，不應未讀就把它擱置。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再表達應先檢視而非未考慮就擱置。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：客人表示收到的包裹少了一件商品，店員想未查包裝紀錄便說客人記錯。你建議先看資料再回應。用一至兩句英文表達，不先判定任何人有錯。

examples.en: We should not brush aside the customer’s report before checking the packing records. The missing item needs a proper review.
examples.zh: 我們不應未查包裝紀錄便擱置客人報告。缺少的商品需要妥善覆核。

examples.en: Rather than brush aside the complaint, let us compare the order with the packing records and then explain what we find.
examples.zh: 與其未認真考慮就擱置投訴，不如比較訂單與包裝紀錄，再解釋發現。

writing.selfCheckZh: 要求先查資料及回應，不把暫時未同意客人就當作輕視，也不預判客人或店員說錯。

takeaways.en: The panel brushed aside the request without discussing its reasons.
takeaways.zh: 小組未討論理由便把要求擱置。

takeaways.en: The panel brushed aside the concern without hearing the members’ reasons.
takeaways.zh: 小組未聽成員理由，就把疑慮擱置。

titleZh: 為省事而省略必要標準

brief.meaningEn: Save time, money or effort by skipping work or standards that are needed.
brief.meaningZh: 為省時間、金錢或力氣，而省略必要工序或標準。
brief.grammar: cut corners on/in something; cut is unchanged in the past.
brief.boundaryZh: 有效簡化而仍符合必要標準，不一定是 cut corners；需指出被省掉的責任。
brief.misconceptionZh: 快不必然等於差；關鍵是是否省略對品質或責任必要的部分。
brief.outcomeZh: 能區分正當效率改善與不妥地省略必要工作。

listening.en: To meet the deadline, they cut corners by skipping the name checks, and several certificates were printed incorrectly.
listening.zh: 為趕限期，他們省略姓名查核來省事，結果幾張證書印錯。
listening.promptZh: 哪個做法是問題？

options.en: They used a shorter form while checking every required name.
options.zh: 他們用較短表格，仍查核每個必要姓名。

options.en: They postponed printing until every name was confirmed.
options.zh: 他們延後印刷，直到每個姓名確認。

options.en: They skipped a necessary check to save time.
options.zh: 他們為省時間而省略必要查核。

options.en: They spent longer discussing the typeface after checking the names.
options.zh: 核對姓名後，他們花較久討論字體。

listening.explanationZh: by skipping name checks 說明省略必要步驟；錯印是題述實際後果。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼這次趕工後證書有錯？
reply.promptEn: Why were there errors in the certificates after the rush?

options.en: They cut corners by leaving out the name checks.
options.zh: 他們為省事而省略姓名查核。

options.en: They saved time at a step needed for accuracy.
options.zh: 他們在保障準確的必要步驟省了時間。

options.en: The names went to print without the planned verification.
options.zh: 姓名未經原定核實便付印。

options.en: The deadline pressure led them to omit an important review.
options.zh: 限期壓力令他們省掉重要覆核。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋省略查核與錯印的關係；金句使用 cut corners。

scene.promptZh: 你們為趕印海報，決定未核實日期就付印，這項核實原本是必要步驟。哪句貼切？

options.en: We are simplifying the form while retaining every required check.
options.zh: 我們簡化表格，同時保留每項必要查核。

options.en: We are cutting corners by skipping the date check.
options.zh: 我們正省略日期查核來省事。

options.en: We are delaying print until the date is confirmed.
options.zh: 我們延後印刷，直到日期確認。

scene.explanationZh: 題目已指明日期核實必要，省略它是犧牲標準，而不是保留查核的簡化。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個做法最不宜稱為 cut corners？

options.en: Leaving out a required check to finish sooner.
options.zh: 為較早完成而省去必要查核。

options.en: Using unsuitable material without telling the client, to reduce costs.
options.zh: 為減成本而用不合適材料，未告知客戶。

options.en: Removing duplicated paperwork while keeping all required checks.
options.zh: 刪去重複文書，同時保留所有必要查核。

contrast.explanationZh: 去除重複而保留標準，可以是合理效率改善。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說只要流程變快就是 cut corners。哪句最準確？

options.en: Check whether necessary standards are skipped, not just whether the process is quicker.
options.zh: 應查是否省略必要標準，不只看流程是否較快。

options.en: We should slow every stage before identifying which checks are actually necessary.
options.zh: 我們應先把每個階段放慢，之後才辨認哪些查核確實必要。

options.en: Judge the quality from the time taken before checking the required steps.
options.zh: 未查必要步驟就按花多少時間判斷品質。

dialogue.explanationZh: 快慢與省略標準不同；應以必要步驟及品質為判斷根據。

speaking.en: We can simplify the form without cutting corners on the checks.
speaking.zh: 我們可以簡化表格，而不省略必要查核來省事。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再區分合理簡化與犧牲標準。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：學生要錄一段長訪問，原定先作簡短音量測試，有人為趕時間想省略這項必要查核。你建議精簡重複介紹，但保留測試。用一至兩句英文回應。

examples.en: We should not cut corners by skipping the sound test before the long interview. We can shorten the repeated introduction instead.
examples.zh: 我們不應為省事而略過長訪問前的音量測試。可以改為縮短重複介紹。

examples.en: Cutting corners on the required sound check may waste the recording; a shorter introduction would save time without removing that check.
examples.zh: 在必要音量查核上偷工減料，可能浪費錄音；較短介紹可省時，而不刪去查核。

writing.selfCheckZh: 分清省略必要查核與精簡重複介紹；不要因較快就一概叫 cut corners。

takeaways.en: Tight deadlines do not excuse cutting corners on essential checks.
takeaways.zh: 限期緊迫不能成為省略必要查核的理由。

takeaways.en: A simpler process can save time without cutting corners.
takeaways.zh: 較簡單流程可以省時間，而不省略必要標準。

titleEn: a matter of life and death

brief.meaningEn: An issue where people’s survival is genuinely at stake; sometimes used hyperbolically for urgency.
brief.meaningZh: 真正涉及人的生存的重大事情；有時也被誇張用作形容迫切。
brief.grammar: be a matter of life and death; not a matter of life and death can put a minor problem in perspective.
brief.register: Strong established expression; distinguish serious literal stakes from exaggeration.
brief.boundaryZh: 本課以虛構情節理解語言，不提供急救或救援程序。緊張不必等於真正生死攸關。
brief.misconceptionZh: 錯選字體或一般延誤，若沒有生存風險背景，不應自動當作真正生死問題。
brief.outcomeZh: 能按具體後果判斷嚴重性，分清字面重大與誇張。

listening.en: In the film, reaching the stranded climbers before the storm was a matter of life and death, not just a question of keeping the schedule.
listening.zh: 電影中，暴風前到達受困攀山者身邊，是生死攸關，不只是守時間表的問題。
listening.promptZh: 電影把事情描述得多嚴重？

options.en: The storm may cause discomfort, but the climbers’ survival is not at stake.
options.zh: 暴風可能造成不適，但攀山者生存未受威脅。

options.en: People’s survival is at stake in the story.
options.zh: 故事中人的生存面臨風險。

options.en: Only the planned arrival time is affected; the climbers are already safe.
options.zh: 只有預定到達時間受影響；攀山者已安全。

options.en: The danger has already caused deaths, rather than putting survival at risk.
options.zh: 危險已造成死亡，而不是讓生存面臨風險。

listening.explanationZh: life and death 表示情節中的生存風險；不只是時間或不適，也不表示死亡已發生。

reply.promptZh: 電影中，為甚麼角色急着在暴風前到達？
reply.promptEn: Why are the characters in the film urgently trying to arrive before the storm?

options.en: The stranded people’s survival may depend on timely help.
options.zh: 受困人士的生存可能依靠及時幫助。

options.en: The consequences go far beyond a late appointment.
options.zh: 後果遠超遲到一次約會。

options.en: It is a matter of life and death in the story.
options.zh: 故事中，這是生死攸關的事情。

options.en: They are responding to a serious danger to the climbers.
options.zh: 他們正回應攀山者面對的嚴重危險。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明虛構情節的重大後果；金句使用本課表達而不提供程序。

scene.promptZh: 小說明確寫出受困人物若得不到及時幫助可能無法生存。哪句準確概括情節的重大性？

options.en: It is a matter of life and death.
options.zh: 這是生死攸關的事情。

options.en: The situation affects the characters’ comfort, but not their survival.
options.zh: 情況影響人物舒適程度，卻不影響生存。

options.en: The characters are already safe, and the only concern is a delayed journey.
options.zh: 人物已安全，唯一疑慮是旅程延誤。

scene.explanationZh: 題目明確提供可能無法生存的風險，不是只有舒適或在已安全下旅程延誤。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持字面上的 a matter of life and death？

options.en: A fictional scene explicitly places stranded people’s survival at risk.
options.zh: 虛構場景明確讓受困人物面對生存風險。

options.en: A harmless title-font choice can be revised later, with no danger to anyone.
options.zh: 無害的標題字體選擇之後可改，沒有任何人的危險。

options.en: A story makes timely help crucial to whether endangered characters survive.
options.zh: 故事把及時幫助設定為遇險人物能否生存的關鍵。

contrast.explanationZh: 無危險、可稍後改的字體選擇，不提供真正生死後果。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友因一個已可更正的小錯字而說「a matter of life and death」。你想辨別是否誇張。哪句最有用？

options.en: Let us assume survival is at risk because the phrase sounds urgent.
options.zh: 片語聽來緊急，我們就假定有生存風險。

options.en: Could we treat the typo as an emergency before checking what it affects?
options.zh: 未查錯字影響甚麼，我們可否先當緊急事故？

options.en: What serious consequences are involved, or are you using the phrase to exaggerate the pressure?
options.zh: 涉及甚麼嚴重後果？還是你用片語誇張描述壓力？

dialogue.explanationZh: 要按後果判斷字面或誇張，不能只靠迫切語氣推定危險。

speaking.en: In the story, the decision is a matter of life and death.
speaking.zh: 故事中，那個決定攸關生死。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把強烈說法放回有生存後果的情節。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：科幻小說明確設定，太空站的空氣系統若不能維持，站內人物可能無法生存。他們正討論維持系統的重要性，不只是舒適或預算。用一至兩句英文評論情節的重大性，不寫維修程序。

examples.en: In the novel, keeping the station’s air system working is a matter of life and death, not merely comfort.
examples.zh: 小說中，維持太空站空氣系統運作是生死攸關，而非只關乎舒適。

examples.en: The characters’ survival depends on the air system, so its continued operation is a matter of life and death in this story.
examples.zh: 人物生存依靠空氣系統，所以在這故事中，系統持續運作是生死攸關。

writing.selfCheckZh: 依小說明確生存設定使用強烈表達，不把一般不便或真實維修細節混入。

takeaways.en: In the novel, finding help becomes a matter of life and death.
takeaways.zh: 小說中，找到幫助變得生死攸關。

takeaways.en: A minor typo is not a matter of life and death; we can correct it calmly.
takeaways.zh: 小錯字不是生死攸關的事；我們可以平靜更正。

brief.meaningEn: Available for discussion, consideration or negotiation.
brief.meaningZh: 仍可供討論、考慮或協商。
brief.grammar: an option/proposal is/remains on the table; put something on the table introduces it for consideration.
brief.boundaryZh: 列入考慮不等於已批准或一定採用，也不需要實物放在桌上。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可同時有多項方案；被提出與最後選中是不同階段。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述仍在考慮中的方案，分清候選與定案。

listening.en: Two venues are still on the table, but the committee has not chosen either one yet.
listening.zh: 兩個場地仍在考慮之列，但委員會還未選定任何一個。
listening.promptZh: 兩個場地的狀態是甚麼？

options.en: Both have already been booked as the final choice.
options.zh: 兩者都已被預訂為最後選擇。

options.en: They remain options for consideration.
options.zh: 它們仍是可考慮選項。

options.en: Both have been rejected and cannot be discussed again.
options.zh: 兩者已被拒絕，不能再討論。

options.en: One venue has already been ruled out, although the final choice is postponed.
options.zh: 其中一個場地已被排除，雖然最後選擇押後了。

listening.explanationZh: still on the table 加 not chosen yet，清楚區分可考慮與已選定。

reply.promptZh: 委員會現在還在考慮哪些場地？
reply.promptEn: Which venues is the committee still considering?

options.en: The hall and the studio are still on the table.
options.zh: 禮堂與工作室仍在考慮之列。

options.en: Both the hall and the studio remain possible options.
options.zh: 禮堂及工作室兩者仍是可能選項。

options.en: We have not ruled out either of those two venues.
options.zh: 我們還未排除那兩個場地中的任何一個。

options.en: The final choice has not been made between the hall and the studio.
options.zh: 禮堂與工作室之間還未作最後選擇。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述未排除的候選場地；金句使用比喻。

scene.promptZh: 小組保留早場與午場兩個方案，未決定採用哪個。哪句準確？

options.en: Both options have been rejected already.
options.zh: 兩個方案都已拒絕。

options.en: The morning session has been confirmed as the only option.
options.zh: 早場已確認為唯一方案。

options.en: Both options are still on the table.
options.zh: 兩個方案仍在考慮之列。

scene.explanationZh: 保留候選不等於排除或確認其中一個。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 an option is still on the table？

options.en: It remains available for discussion.
options.zh: 它仍可討論。

options.en: It has been formally withdrawn and is no longer available for consideration.
options.zh: 它已正式撤回，不再可供考慮。

options.en: The group has not yet ruled it out.
options.zh: 小組還未排除它。

contrast.explanationZh: 正式撤回而不再可考慮，與仍在桌上作候選的比喻不同。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友把「方案 on the table」寫成已確定執行。哪句澄清最準確？

options.en: It is available for consideration, but we still need a decision before treating it as approved.
options.zh: 它可供考慮，但仍需作決定才可當作批准。

options.en: Could we reserve it as final before asking whether the other options remain?
options.zh: 未問其他選項是否仍在，我們可否先把它定為最後？

options.en: The proposal’s presence in the discussion should replace the approval step.
options.zh: 提案出現在討論中，應取代批准步驟。

dialogue.explanationZh: 被提出與批准是不同階段，不能用候選狀態代替決定。

speaking.en: Several proposals remain on the table while the team compares their costs.
speaking.zh: 團隊比較費用時，幾項提案仍在考慮之列。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再表達候選而未定案的狀態。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：課堂植物調查中，小組仍在比較「光線不足」與「澆水頻率不合」兩個可能解釋，尚無測試可排除任何一個。用一至兩句英文說明兩個假設仍可考慮，並非已證實。

examples.en: Both explanations are still on the table because the group has not tested the light level or watering frequency yet.
examples.zh: 兩個解釋仍在考慮之列，因為小組尚未測試光線或澆水頻率。

examples.en: Low light remains on the table as one possible explanation, alongside watering frequency; neither has been confirmed.

writing.selfCheckZh: 保留仍可討論與尚未證實的差別，不把候選解釋當作已選定原因。

listening.en: The supervisor knew the same error was affecting customers but turned a blind eye to avoid delaying the launch.
listening.zh: 主管知道相同錯誤正影響顧客，卻為免延遲推出而故意不理。
listening.promptZh: 哪點使這是 turn a blind eye？

options.en: The supervisor had not yet received any report of the error.
options.zh: 主管還未收到錯誤報告。

options.en: The supervisor was investigating before deciding what had happened.
options.zh: 主管正在調查，才決定發生了甚麼。

options.en: The supervisor knew about the problem and chose not to address it.
options.zh: 主管知道問題，卻選擇不處理。

options.en: The customers had already confirmed that the error was fixed.
options.zh: 顧客已確認錯誤修好。

listening.explanationZh: knew 與 avoid delaying 提供知情及有意不處理的背景，不是未察覺。

reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼批評主管對錯誤的反應？
reply.promptEn: Why are you critical of the supervisor’s response to the error?

options.en: The supervisor knew customers were affected but chose not to act.
options.zh: 主管知道顧客受影響，卻選擇不行動。

options.en: The supervisor turned a blind eye to the repeated error.
options.zh: 主管對反覆錯誤故意不理。

options.en: Avoiding a delay was given priority over addressing a known problem.
options.zh: 避免延遲被放在處理已知問題之前。

options.en: The reports were understood, but the fault was knowingly left unresolved.
options.zh: 報告已被理解，但故障明知未解決仍被留下。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明明知卻不處理；金句用本課表達概括。

scene.promptZh: 主辦者已確認錯誤日期仍在公開告示，卻為免麻煩決定不修改、不通知。哪句合適？

options.en: They are turning a blind eye to a known problem.
options.zh: 他們正對已知問題故意不理。

options.en: They have not yet learned that the date is wrong.
options.zh: 他們還未得知日期錯了。

options.en: They are checking the report before deciding whether the date needs changing.
options.zh: 他們正查報告，才決定日期是否需改。

scene.explanationZh: 已確認仍有錯、卻決定不處理，提供故意忽略而非未察覺或調查中的背景。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 turn a blind eye？

options.en: Someone knows the published detail is wrong but deliberately leaves it unchanged.
options.zh: 某人知道發布資料錯誤，卻故意不改。

options.en: Someone receives a report and promptly checks it before making a judgement.
options.zh: 某人收到報告後立即查核，再作判斷。

options.en: A manager understands the complaint but chooses to ignore it to avoid work.
options.zh: 經理明白投訴，卻為省工作而選擇忽略。

contrast.explanationZh: 及時查核是處理問題，不是明知故意不理。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說只因錯誤沒即時修好，就一定是 turn a blind eye。哪個回應較準確？

options.en: The delay alone is enough to conclude that they deliberately ignored the error.
options.zh: 單憑延誤已足以斷定他們故意忽略錯誤。

options.en: We can leave the investigation notes out because the repair was slow.
options.zh: 因修復緩慢，我們可以略去調查紀錄。

options.en: Did they know about it and deliberately ignore it, or were they still investigating?
options.zh: 他們是知情而故意忽略，還是仍在調查？

dialogue.explanationZh: 故意忽略需要知情及選擇不理；修復速度本身不足以證明動機。

speaking.en: We should not turn a blind eye to an error we know is affecting readers.
speaking.zh: 我們不應對已知正影響讀者的錯誤故意不理。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再保留知情而選擇忽略的核心意思。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：美術組已確認展板用了一位同學的插圖卻沒列名，有人因怕延誤而想明知不理。你希望補上應有署名。用一至兩句英文建議，不指控未知動機。

examples.en: We should not turn a blind eye to the missing credit now that we know whose illustration it is. Let us add the artist’s name.
examples.zh: 既然知道插圖是誰的，我們不應對漏署名視而不見。把創作者名字補上吧。

examples.en: Turning a blind eye would leave a known credit problem unresolved; we should acknowledge the student before displaying the work.
examples.zh: 視而不見會讓已知署名問題未解決；我們應在展示作品前列出那位學生。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用已知而故意不理作判斷，提出補署名；不要只因修正需時就推斷有人故意忽略。

takeaways.en: The manager turned a blind eye to a problem she already understood.
takeaways.zh: 經理對已明白的問題故意不理。

takeaways.en: Checking a concern is different from turning a blind eye to it.
takeaways.zh: 查核疑慮與對它故意不理不同。

listening.en: Requests for evening opening hours have become hard to ignore, so the library is checking whether a later closing time is practical.
listening.zh: 延長晚間開放的要求已變得難以忽視，所以圖書館正查核延後關門是否可行。
listening.promptZh: 圖書館目前怎樣回應要求？

options.en: It sees a clear demand and is examining whether a change is workable.
options.zh: 它看見明確需求，正檢視改動是否可行。

options.en: It has already extended every evening’s opening hours.
options.zh: 它已延長每晚開放時間。

options.en: It has concluded that visitors no longer want evening access.
options.zh: 它已斷定訪客不再需要晚間使用。

options.en: It is checking whether the requests concern earlier morning opening.
options.zh: 它正查核要求是否有關清晨提早開放。

listening.explanationZh: 要求已明顯到不能略過；is checking 表示仍在查可行性，未等於已實行。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼圖書館需要認真研究晚間開放？
reply.promptEn: Why should the library seriously consider evening opening?

options.en: Many visitors have asked for access after work.
options.zh: 許多訪客要求下班後仍可使用。

options.en: The demand for evening access is hard to ignore.
options.zh: 晚間使用的需求大得難以忽視。

options.en: The repeated requests show that the current hours leave a need unmet.
options.zh: 重複要求顯示現有時間未能滿足一項需要。

options.en: The number of people asking suggests a change deserves consideration.
options.zh: 提出要求的人數顯示改動值得考慮。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋研究需求的原因；金句用 hard to ignore 表示需求值得注意。

scene.promptZh: 社區調查持續收到不少長者對階梯出入口的意見；未決定工程，管理員先研究可用改善方案。哪句最準確？

options.en: The concern is hard to ignore, although the response is still being assessed.
options.zh: 疑慮已難以忽視，雖然應對方法仍在評估。

options.en: The survey shows that access has already been improved.
options.zh: 調查顯示出入口已改善。

options.en: The comments mainly ask the team to keep the entrance unchanged.
options.zh: 意見主要要求小組保持出入口不變。

scene.explanationZh: 持續意見支持問題值得注意，但未提供工程已完成或無需改動的證據。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句把 hard to ignore 的意思說得過頭？

options.en: These repeated reports make the issue deserve attention.
options.zh: 反覆報告讓問題值得注意。

options.en: A noticeable improvement can be hard to ignore too.
options.zh: 明顯進步也可以難以忽視。

options.en: Calling the evidence hard to ignore settles which remedy we must use.
options.zh: 說證據難以忽視，就已決定必須用哪個解法。

contrast.explanationZh: 證據值得注意與選定解法是不同判斷；仍需研究可行方案。

dialogue.promptZh: 同學說「意見 hard to ignore，所以新的開放時間已經定了」。哪句澄清最合適？

options.en: We should announce the new hours before the feasibility review ends.
options.zh: 可行性覆核完成前，我們應宣布新時間。

options.en: The demand deserves attention, but the library is still checking what it can offer.
options.zh: 需求值得注意，但圖書館仍在查能提供甚麼。

options.en: Let us treat the requests as approval of the staffing plan.
options.zh: 把這些要求當作人手方案已獲批准吧。

dialogue.explanationZh: 明確需求不等於已批准具體時間或人手方案。

speaking.en: The repeated requests are hard to ignore, but we still need a workable plan.
speaking.zh: 重複要求已難以忽視，但我們仍需可行計劃。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出值得注意的需求及下一步。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：合唱團連續幾次錄音顯示節奏比上月整齊，連原本懷疑的同學也留意進步。你想肯定明顯改善，但仍會聽錄音找下一步。用一至兩句英文描述。

examples.en: The improvement in our timing is hard to ignore after several recordings, though we still need to listen for the next areas to improve.
examples.zh: 幾次錄音後，節奏進步已難以忽視，雖然我們仍需聽下一步可改善處。

examples.en: Our steadier rhythm is hard to ignore, even to the doubtful singers; reviewing the recordings can help us build on it.
examples.zh: 我們較穩定的節奏已難以忽視，連懷疑的團員也察覺；回顧錄音可幫我們再進步。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用多次錄音支持正面變化明顯，保留仍可查核及改善，不把它變成已完美。

takeaways.en: A clear improvement can be hard to ignore.
takeaways.zh: 明顯進步可以讓人難以忽視。

takeaways.en: The complaints are hard to ignore, but we need evidence before choosing a response.
takeaways.zh: 投訴已難以忽視，但選擇應對前我們需要證據。

brief.meaningEn: The feeling, mood or expressive richness that gives an experience or work its character.
brief.meaningZh: 令作品或經驗具有個性的感受、氣氛及表達層次。
brief.grammar: give/add emotional colour to a scene, story or experience; colour is uncountable in this use.
brief.register: Descriptive figurative wording, often used about art and experience; British spelling colour.
brief.boundaryZh: 可以有喜悅、懷念、緊張或混合感受，不限悲傷；本課不是實際可見的顏色。
brief.misconceptionZh: 改變觀眾感受不等於改變劇情事實；豐富情感也不必等於更大聲。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說明表演、音樂或細節怎樣增加情感層次。

listening.en: The quiet piano gave the reunion scene emotional colour, bringing warmth to a conversation that was otherwise quite plain.
listening.zh: 輕柔鋼琴為重聚場景添上情感色彩，讓原本平淡的對話多了溫暖。
listening.promptZh: 鋼琴在場景中有甚麼作用？

options.en: It changed the dialogue into a different account of how the people met.
options.zh: 它把對話改成另一段相識經過。

options.en: It made the plain conversation feel warmer.
options.zh: 它讓平淡對話感覺更溫暖。

options.en: It made the reunion feel colder and more distant.
options.zh: 它讓重聚顯得更冷淡疏遠。

options.en: It supplied missing facts about the characters’ family history.
options.zh: 它補充角色家族史中缺少的事實。

listening.explanationZh: bringing warmth 解釋情感效果，不是補充身世或改寫故事事實。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你覺得重聚場景比原本對話更動人？
reply.promptEn: Why did the reunion feel more moving than the plain dialogue?

options.en: The quiet piano brought warmth to it.
options.zh: 輕柔鋼琴令它更溫暖。

options.en: The music made the characters’ affection easier to feel.
options.zh: 音樂讓角色的情誼更易感受到。

options.en: The piano added emotional colour to the scene.
options.zh: 鋼琴為場景添上情感色彩。

options.en: The gentle accompaniment gave the exchange a tender mood.
options.zh: 柔和伴奏讓對話有溫柔氣氛。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述溫柔情感效果；金句使用 emotional colour。

scene.promptZh: 同一句告別，演員放慢並稍停，令觀眾感到不捨；文字沒有改。哪句貼切？

options.en: Her delivery added emotional colour without changing the words.
options.zh: 她的演繹沒改文字，卻增加情感層次。

options.en: Her delivery supplied a new reason for the farewell that the script had omitted.
options.zh: 她的演繹補上劇本遺漏的告別新原因。

options.en: The pause removed the sense of attachment from the farewell.
options.zh: 停頓讓告別不再有依戀感。

scene.explanationZh: 語速與停頓改變情感感受，不是加入新的情節原因。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句最不像 emotional colour 在本課的用法？

options.en: A remembered detail gives the story a wistful mood.
options.zh: 記憶細節讓故事有惆悵氣氛。

options.en: A shift in the actor’s tone reveals mixed feelings.
options.zh: 演員語氣轉變顯示混合感受。

options.en: A factual correction changes which year the event occurred, without affecting its mood.
options.zh: 事實更正改變事件年份，沒有改變氣氛。

contrast.explanationZh: 本課重點是情感及氣氛層次；只有年份事實改動未能說明這種效果。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說 emotional colour 就是把背景音樂調大聲。哪句回應最準確？

options.en: Could we judge the feeling only by the speaker volume?
options.zh: 我們可否只按喇叭音量判斷感受？

options.en: It concerns the feeling the music adds; a quiet passage can be expressive too.
options.zh: 它關乎音樂增添的感受；輕柔段落也可富表達力。

options.en: Let us increase the volume without considering whether it suits the scene.
options.zh: 不考慮是否配合場景，先把音量加大吧。

dialogue.explanationZh: 情感效果要看配合、語氣與氣氛，不可只用音量判斷。

speaking.en: The gentle music added emotional colour to the final scene.
speaking.zh: 柔和音樂為最後場景添上情感色彩。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明音樂怎樣增加感受層次。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為一段祖父母舊照片短片配上輕柔音樂，畫面不變，但更有懷念與溫暖。用一至兩句英文描述效果。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出懷念或溫暖等感受，不把音樂效果寫成照片內容或歷史事實改變。

examples.en: The gentle music gives the old photographs emotional colour, adding warmth and a sense of remembrance.
examples.zh: 柔和音樂為舊照片添上情感色彩，增加溫暖與懷念。

examples.en: We kept the images unchanged, but the soft accompaniment added emotional colour to the short film.
examples.zh: 我們保持影像不變，但柔和伴奏為短片增加情感層次。

takeaways.en: Small details can give a story emotional colour.
takeaways.zh: 小細節可以為故事添上情感色彩。

takeaways.en: Emotional colour can come from a quiet voice as well as from music.
takeaways.zh: 輕柔聲音與音樂都可以帶來情感層次。

titleZh: 緊密融入生活或文化肌理

brief.meaningEn: Closely integrated into the interconnected activities, relationships or culture of a community.
brief.meaningZh: 緊密融入社群互相連繫的活動、人際往來或文化之中。
brief.grammar: be woven into the fabric of everyday life; be woven into the cultural fabric. Woven is the past participle of weave. Everyday life adds a particular focus on ordinary routines; cultural fabric can include recurring customs that are not daily.
brief.register: Extended fabric-as-interconnected-life metaphor. Identify the practices and relationships supporting the integration claim.
brief.boundaryZh: 融入不表示每人都做或從此不變；of everyday life需日常情境根據，cultural fabric可包括非每日的反覆習俗。這裏不是實際編織。
brief.misconceptionZh: 一次活動不自動證已緊密融入社群；需看持續、反覆及與其他生活部分的連結，不把文化重要等同每日出現。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體活動及人際連結支持融入生活或文化的說法，分日常頻率與文化整合。

options.en: The song persuaded me to agree with every view the singer holds.

titleEn: someone’s cup of tea / not everyone’s cup of tea
titleZh: 合某人口味／未必合每個人口味

target.pattern: (?:\bnot (?:everyone[’']s|my|your|his|her|our|their) cup of tea\b)|(?:\b(?:is|are|was|were) (?:my|your|his|her|our|their) cup of tea\b)

brief.meaningEn: A personal preference: affirmative be someone’s cup of tea means they enjoy it; the negative form means they do not or that tastes differ.
brief.meaningZh: 形容個人喜好：肯定形式表示合某人口味；否定形式表示某人不喜歡，或並非人人都喜歡。
brief.grammar: be someone’s cup of tea means they enjoy it; not someone’s cup of tea means they do not; not everyone’s cup of tea means some may dislike it, not that nobody enjoys it.
brief.register: Common conversational idiom, often a polite way to express preference.
brief.boundaryZh: 肯定 their 表示該群體喜歡，不代表人人喜歡；not everyone 並非沒有人喜歡；not their 指指定群體。談喜好不等於客觀判斷品質。
brief.misconceptionZh: 自己不喜歡不表示作品差；部分人不喜歡也不表示大部分人都反對。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用肯定與否定形式表達喜好差異，正確保留 everyone 與特定群體的範圍。

options.en: Its quiet pace suits some people more than others.
options.zh: 它安靜的節奏比較適合某些人。

options.en: My friends have different tastes in films.
options.zh: 我的朋友對電影有不同喜好。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以喜好差異解釋推薦範圍；金句不表示無人喜歡。

scene.promptZh: 你喜歡安靜的博物館，朋友則愛熱鬧活動。你想禮貌說這次靜態展覽未必人人適合。哪句最好？

options.en: A quiet exhibition is not everyone’s cup of tea, though I enjoy it.
options.zh: 安靜展覽未必合每個人的口味，雖然我喜歡。

options.en: Because I enjoy quiet exhibitions, this one must suit all my friends.
options.zh: 因為我喜歡安靜展覽，這個就必定適合我所有朋友。

options.en: Our different preferences establish that the exhibition is poorly made.
options.zh: 我們的喜好不同，證明展覽製作差。

scene.explanationZh: 喜好可以不同，不可由自己的偏好推及全部朋友或品質。

contrast.promptZh: 同學談到歷史學會時說「Community-history work is their cup of tea」。哪個理解最準確？

options.en: The history club enjoys community-history work.
options.zh: 歷史學會喜歡社區歷史工作。

options.en: The history club dislikes community-history work.
options.zh: 歷史學會不喜歡社區歷史工作。

options.en: The speaker has proved that every student enjoys community-history work.
options.zh: 說話者證明每位學生都喜歡社區歷史工作。

contrast.explanationZh: 肯定形式 is their cup of tea 表示歷史學會喜歡這類工作，不代表每位學生都喜歡。

dialogue.promptZh: 同學說「not everyone’s cup of tea 就是沒有觀眾喜歡」。哪句澄清最準確？

options.en: Could we replace some differing tastes with a conclusion about every viewer?
options.zh: 我們可否把部分喜好不同，換成對每位觀眾的結論？

options.en: Let us use one friend’s dislike as the audience-wide verdict.
options.zh: 把一位朋友不喜歡當作全體觀眾的結論吧。

options.en: It is not everyone’s cup of tea: some people may dislike it, while others can still enjoy it.
options.zh: 它未必合每個人的口味：部分人可能不喜歡，但其他人仍可欣賞。

dialogue.explanationZh: not everyone 否定人人都喜歡，並非肯定人人都不喜歡。

speaking.en: Quiet films are not everyone’s cup of tea, but I enjoy their slower pace.
speaking.zh: 安靜電影未必合每個人的口味，但我喜歡它們較慢的節奏。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再溫和說明個人偏好與別人可能不同。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你喜歡周末看長篇紀錄片，但朋友中有些人較愛短喜劇。用一至兩句英文說明你喜歡，同時不假設人人有相同口味。
writing.selfCheckZh: 保留部分喜好不同及自己喜歡，不把 not everyone 寫成沒有人欣賞。

examples.en: Long documentaries are not everyone’s cup of tea, but I enjoy watching them at the weekend.
examples.zh: 長篇紀錄片未必合每個人的口味，但我喜歡周末觀看。

examples.en: This long documentary is not everyone’s cup of tea. Some of my friends prefer short comedies, while I enjoy a detailed account.
examples.zh: 這部長篇紀錄片未必合每個人的口味。部分朋友較愛短喜劇，我則喜歡詳細敘述。

takeaways.en: Experimental theatre is not everyone’s cup of tea.
takeaways.zh: 實驗劇場未必合每個人的口味。

takeaways.en: Local history is her cup of tea, so she volunteered to guide the archive tour.
takeaways.zh: 本地歷史很合她的興趣，所以她自願帶領檔案館導賞。

titleZh: 生活瑣事打亂原定計劃

brief.meaningEn: Ordinary demands or unexpected events interrupt plans or make them difficult to carry out.
brief.meaningZh: 平常事務或突發事情打斷計劃，令原定安排難以實行。
brief.grammar: life gets in the way of plans; past life got in the way; a broad explanation often needs concrete context.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是所有生活都成為障礙，也不表示計劃永遠不可能；說明原因後仍可道歉、協調及重新安排。
brief.misconceptionZh: 用這句解釋延誤不會自動消除責任；不能由一句話推斷對方沒有重視承諾。
brief.outcomeZh: 能具體解釋生活事務打斷安排，並提出可行下一步。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: We meant to meet more often, but life gets in the way.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 1, table 1, row 8; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: We planned a weekly catch-up, but life got in the way when our work shifts changed and we had family commitments, so we are finding a new time.
listening.zh: 我們原定每周聚會，但輪班改動及家庭安排打亂了計劃，所以正找新時間。
listening.promptZh: 每周聚會出了甚麼情況？

options.en: The friends decided they no longer valued spending time together.
options.zh: 朋友們決定不再重視相聚。

options.en: Work and family demands interrupted the plan, and they are trying to rearrange it.
options.zh: 工作與家庭事務打斷計劃，他們正嘗試另作安排。

options.en: The weekly meeting went ahead at its original time without difficulty.
options.zh: 每周聚會如期在原定時間順利舉行。

options.en: They had never agreed to meet before discussing the work shifts.
options.zh: 討論輪班前，他們從未約定聚會。

listening.explanationZh: life got in the way 由輪班及家庭事務具體解釋；找新時間顯示仍想相聚。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你們未能繼續原定的每周聚會？
reply.promptEn: Why could you not keep the weekly catch-up at the agreed time?

options.en: Our changing work shifts made the usual time difficult.
options.zh: 我們改動的輪班讓原定時間難以配合。

options.en: Family commitments clashed with the time we had chosen.
options.zh: 家庭安排與我們選定的時間衝突。

options.en: Life got in the way when work and family demands increased.
options.zh: 工作與家庭事務增加，生活事務打亂了計劃。

options.en: Several everyday responsibilities left us unable to keep that slot.
options.zh: 幾項日常責任令我們無法保留那個時段。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都具體交代阻礙安排的原因；金句用 life got in the way 概括。

scene.promptZh: 你原定每天練習攝影，但這周加班及照顧家人，幾次未能練習。你仍想繼續，計劃周末補練。哪句貼切？

options.en: Life got in the way this week, but I am setting aside time to practise at the weekend.
options.zh: 這周生活事務打亂計劃，但我正留時間周末練習。

options.en: I practised at the agreed time every day, so the schedule did not change.
options.zh: 我每天都在原定時間練習，所以時間表沒有改。

options.en: I abandoned photography because I discovered I had no interest in it.
options.zh: 我發現自己對攝影毫無興趣，所以放棄了。

scene.explanationZh: 加班及照顧打斷習慣，但周末補練表示未放棄興趣。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句把 life gets in the way 的含意說得過頭？

options.en: Everyday responsibilities can interrupt a plan.
options.zh: 日常責任可以打斷計劃。

options.en: The person may need to revise the arrangement.
options.zh: 當事人可能需要修改安排。

options.en: The interruption means rescheduling is pointless and the commitment no longer matters.
options.zh: 計劃被打斷就表示重新安排沒有意義，承諾也不再重要。

contrast.explanationZh: 生活事務可令安排暫時困難，不等於永遠無法再約或責任消失。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友錯過約定後說 life got in the way，想就此不再聯絡。哪句建議最合適？

options.en: Could the broad explanation replace telling the other person whether we will rearrange it?
options.zh: 籠統解釋可否代替告訴對方是否另約？

options.en: Explain the specific difficulty, apologise and suggest a time you can keep.
options.zh: 解釋具體困難、道歉，並提出能遵守的時間。

options.en: Let us assume the other person knows which work commitment caused the delay.
options.zh: 假定對方知道哪項工作安排造成延誤吧。

dialogue.explanationZh: 解釋生活阻礙後仍要溝通、承擔影響與提出可行安排。

speaking.en: Life got in the way this week, so let us choose a time we can both keep.
speaking.zh: 這周生活事務打亂了計劃，一起選個大家都能遵守的時間吧。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再解釋安排受阻並提出重新協調。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你原想這個月寫完短篇故事，卻因突然搬家，要打包及整理住處而耽擱。你仍想完成，打算安頓後每次寫一段。用一至兩句英文解釋中斷及下一步。

examples.en: Life got in the way of finishing my story when an unexpected move took up my evenings. Once settled, I will restart one paragraph at a time.
examples.zh: 突然搬家佔去晚上時間，生活事務打亂了完成故事的計劃。安頓後，我會每次寫一段重新開始。

examples.en: I meant to finish the short story this month, but life got in the way with packing and settling into a new home. I still plan to continue in small steps.
examples.zh: 我本想這個月寫完短篇故事，但打包及安頓新居等生活事務打亂計劃。我仍打算逐小步繼續。

glossary.en: packing and settling into a new home

writing.selfCheckZh: 具體交代搬家事務中斷創作，保留仍想完成及較小可行下一步，不當作永久放棄。

takeaways.en: We meant to practise together, but life got in the way.
takeaways.zh: 我們本想一起練習，但生活事務打亂了計劃。

takeaways.en: When life gets in the way, a smaller plan may help us start again.
takeaways.zh: 生活事務打亂計劃時，較小的計劃或能幫助我們重新開始。
